chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abdullah ibn Bahrr from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is lazy or weakens and prays the voluntary prayer sitting, he said: 'He gives the reward of two rak'ahs for one rak'ah.'

key_terms.يُضَعِّفُ: He is given double the reward

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for voluntary prayers performed sitting due to weakness or laziness?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'ta'deel' (equating) is applied to voluntary prayers, granting a multiplier of two rewards for each rak'ah performed while sitting due to weakness or laziness. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that reduced physical exertion in worship is compensated by increased spiritual reward, encouraging consistency in nafl prayers even when one's capacity is diminished.
